newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says consumption rise not just car effect.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says consumption rise not just car effect.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Friday the growth in household consumption this year was not just the result of increased purchases of cars.
Speaking at a meeting of the Caisse Nationale de Credit Agricole group, Arthuis said consumption was up 3.3 percent in the first nine months of the year compared with the same period a year earlier.
"It's not only a question of a car effect as retail sales rose 1.7 percent in the same period," said Arthuis.
Car sales in France have been boosted by a government incentive scheme which came to an end last month.
Arthuis repeated that the French public deficit as a percentage of gross domestic product would be below three percent in 1997 and below two percent from 2001.
He also said French banks were not sufficiently profitable and called on them to increase their efforts to reduce costs.
